html:
The Hejaz Railway was a narrow-gauge line built by the Ottoman Empire from Damascus to Medina in the Hejaz, opened in 1908.

Sultan Abdul Hamid II launched it in 1900 to carry pilgrims to the holy cities, and also to tie distant Arabia to Istanbul and move troops quickly. It was paid for largely by gifts from Muslims across the world, which gave it a religious glow and helped the sultan's claim as caliph. A planned extension to Mecca was never built.

The trip from Damascus to Medina fell from about forty days by camel caravan to a few days. But Bedouin who earned a living guarding and supplying caravans saw it as a threat.

In the First World War, fighters of the Arab Revolt, with the British officer T. E. Lawrence, blew up track and trains again and again. The southern line never ran again; parts survive in Jordan and Syria.
sum: The Hejaz Railway was a narrow-gauge line built by the Ottoman Empire from Damascus to Medina in the Hejaz, opened in 1908.
